equivalents.note: The Tibetan line has gzugs brnyan, 'reflection', for adaśa jaisā, 'like a mirror'; the comment (m2) has me long for the mirror itself.
The refrain's māṇā (manas) is yid here, where cia in 5a is sems.
The Tibetan has rgyun mi 'chad, 'its stream is not cut off', reading the cutting as a break in continuity ('chad also means 'explain', so it is not searchable).
The Tibetan line reads 'deluded about illusion' (sgyu ma la rmongs) and goes on to white hair and wrinkles (skra dkar gnyer), apparently taking bali bali as valī-palita, 'wrinkles and grey hair'.
The verse line has de nyid, 'thatness', for tathatā; the comment (m6) has the standard de bzhin nyid.
The Tibetan takes ṣohia as an imperative, 'purify!' (sbyang bar gyis), addressed to the hearer.
The Tibetan has rmi lam gyi skyes bu, 'the person in a dream', where the Sanskrit has svapne svapratibhāsa, 'one's own appearance in a dream'.
The Tibetan has no word for the mārga of sadguruvacanamārga, 'the path of the true guru's word'.
The vocative bho anadhigatamārga, 'you who have not reached the path', becomes a condition, gal te khyod kyis lam ma rtogs na, 'if you have not understood the path'.
The comment has the plain chod par, 'cut', for the weapon's cutting (the string also sits inside mchod pa, 'offering', so it cannot be searched as clear).
The Tibetan splits jñānalocana, 'the eye of knowledge', into shes nas ... mig gis mthong, 'knowing ... they see with the eye'.

equivalents.wylie: phyogs dang phyogs ma yin pa
equivalents.note: The Tibetan has phyogs dang phyogs ma yin pa dbyer med pa, 'side and non-side inseparable', where the Sanskrit has pakṣāpakṣabhinna, 'distinct from side and non-side' (perhaps reading abhinna).

questions: moha (মোহ, cp.46.1b): not matched. The Tibetan line, bar gyi srid pa nyid kyang de bzhin no, 'the intermediate existence too is like that', has no word for delusion; it follows Munidatta's gloss antarā bhavavijñāna (m2) rather than the Bengali antarāle moha. Delusion is matched at 2a and 3b (rmongs).

bridge (সংক্রম, cp.46.m3): not matched, because this is a false hit. The word is vijñānasaṃkramaṇa, the passing of consciousness at death, not a bridge; the Tibetan renders it rnam par shes pas yang dag par 'gro ba, 'consciousness truly going'.

burning and wetting (cp.46.m4) are given from the verse line only. The comment has mes tshig par, 'burnt by fire', and chus khyer bar, 'carried off by water', for jale na plāvanīyam, 'not to be flooded by water'.

Witness flag, not a term (cp.46.m4): in the verse from an outside śāstra the Tibetan fills Shastri's lacuna after puṇyaprasaṅgād api with bsod nams zhar la byung yang spyod mi byed, 'merit, even when it comes their way, they do not practise'. It also reads 'sins' (sdig pa), as if pāpāni, where the Sanskrit has pāryyāṇi.
Pada numbering, not a term: the Sanskrit's dvitīyapadena (m4) and tṛtīyapadena (m5) are rkang pa gsum pas and rkang pa gnyis pas in the Tibetan, so the second and third pada are swapped.
